content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding Single-Field vs Composite Indexes in Firebase Firestore"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"When querying data in Firebase Firestore, understanding how indexes work is critical for performance and cost efficiency. Firestore automatically indexes single fields, but complex queries often require composite indexes."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"What is a Single-Field Index?"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"By default, Firestore automatically creates single-field indexes for every field in a document, as well as for each subfield in a map. These indexes support basic equality and range queries on a single field."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Automatic Creation: Firestore builds single-field indexes out-of-the-box for all document fields."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Query Support: Ideal for filtering by a single property using operators like ==, <, <=, >, >=, or array-contains."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"db.collection('users').where('age', '>', 21).get()"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"What is a Composite Index?"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"A composite index combines multiple fields in a specific order. You must explicitly create composite indexes for queries that filter or sort by more than one field."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Manual Creation: Required when executing queries with multiple where clauses or a mix of where and orderBy clauses on different fields."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Order Sensitivity: The sequence of fields in a composite index matters significantly for query matching."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"db.collection('users').where('age', '>', 21).orderBy('age').orderBy('lastName').get()"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Handling Missing Index Errors"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"If you run a query that requires a composite index that does not yet exist, Firestore will throw an error in your console. The error message will conveniently include a direct URL to automatically generate the missing index in the Firebase Console."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid over-indexing: Only create composite indexes that your application logic actively demands to save storage space."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use equality filters first: Place fields with equality operators (==) before range operators (<, >, in) in your composite index configuration."}]
